entries.title: Background
entries.content: Around noon on 16 July 2024, hundreds of students gathered at Park Mor, the open area adjacent to Gate 1 of Begum Rokeya University, Rangpur, as part of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement. Law enforcers present at the scene first fired tear gas and sound grenades; most students retreated. Among them was Abu Sayed, an English department student and the movement's local coordinator at the university.

entries.title: What Followed
entries.content: Abu Sayed did not retreat with the others; witnesses at the scene describe him standing his ground with arms outstretched, facing the advancing police. The phrase associated with this stance — “Buk petechi, guli kor,” “I have bared my chest — shoot me” — is documented in contemporary reporting. Sources differ on the exact weapon used: Amnesty International's analysis found that police fired shotguns loaded with birdshot at close range; other contemporaneous reporting describes rubber bullets; the findings of a later tribunal describe “multiple gunshot injuries.” The accounts are recorded separately rather than collapsed into a single version. A tribunal later found no lawful or proportionate justification for the use of lethal force, and rejected claims that the killing occurred during an armed confrontation. Abu Sayed was taken to Rangpur Medical College Hospital, where he was declared dead; he was buried the next day, 17 July 2024, in his ancestral village of Babanpur, Pirganj. His death, captured on a widely circulated video, became a defining symbol of the July 2024 uprising. As a separate, subsequent legal development outside the events of 16 July itself, an International Crimes Tribunal in 2026 sentenced two former police officers to death in connection with his killing.
